nodes.name: Pt₃Ni Alloy Formation
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis, 120 mg of K30 was first dissolved in 30 mL of deionized water with magnetic stirring. Then, 3 mL of 2.5 mol L⁻¹ KBr, 0.4 mL of 0.2 mol L⁻¹ H₂PtCl₆ and 0.2 mL of 0.2 mol L⁻¹ NiCl₂ were added to the solution in sequence. After stirring for 30 min, 36 mL of freshly prepared 2 mg mL⁻¹ NaBH₄ aqueous solution was added dropwise to the mixed solution. After stirring for 20 min, the products were obtained through centrifugation and washing with deionized water several times.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 has a sponge structure similar to Pt₃Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images show that NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 has a sponge structure, which is similar to that of Pt₃Ni (Figures S1 and S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals lattice spacings of 0.221 nm and 0.198 nm for Pt₃Ni {111} and {200} planes, and 0.243 nm and 0.209 nm for NiO (111) and (200) planes on the surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic-resolution high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscope (HAADF-STEM) images (Figure 1b; Figure S3) clearly reveal the presence of lattice spacings of 0.221 and 0.198 nm corresponding to the planes that belong to {111} and {200} of Pt₃Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows Ni and O dispersed wider than Pt signal, confirming heterogeneous structure with low NiO content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Analysis of the highlighted area of the energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectrum provides further evidence for the heterogeneous structure of NiO/Pt₃Ni-300, with both Ni and O dispersed wider than the Pt signal.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms Pt₃Ni phase maintenance after calcination; no crystalline NiO peaks in NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 but present in NiO/Pt₃Ni-400.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In comparison with the Pt₃Ni sample, the XRD pattern of NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 confirms the maintenance of the Pt₃Ni phase after calcination. Note the diffraction peaks corresponding to crystalline NiO (ICDD no.65-2901) were observed in NiO/Pt₃Ni-400 but not for NiO/Pt₃Ni-200 and NiO/Pt₃Ni-300.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES confirms Pt:Ni ratio of 3:1 for Pt₃Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Combined with the inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) results of a close Pt:Ni ratio of 3:1 (Table S1), its crystal phase could be confirmed as Pt₃Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS of NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 shows peaks at 532.5 eV (H₂O), 529.8 eV (oxygen near V_O), 528.4 eV (lattice oxygen), 531.5 eV (surface OH); larger oxygen-vacancy defects (70%) than NiO/Pt₃Ni-200 (59%) and NiO/Pt₃Ni-400 (55%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Peaks in the O 1s XPS spectrum of NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 (Figure 1i) can be deconvoluted into four peaks, including three peaks at 532.5, 529.8, and 528.4 eV attributed to H₂O, oxygen in the vicinity of the oxygen defects (V_O), and lattice oxygen (L_O), respectively [25, 26], and a significant peak at 531.5 eV attributed to surface OH [27]. The larger numbers of oxygen-vacancy defects (70%) in NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 compared to those in NiO/Pt₃Ni-200 (59%) reveal that unsaturated NiO is generated.

nodes.characterization_summary: ESR shows stronger Lorentzian line signal for NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 indicating higher unpaired electron content from oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A stronger single Lorentzian line signal is present in the ESR spectrum of NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 (Figure 1j), suggesting that it has a higher unpaired electron content that likely originates from the oxygen vacancy in unsaturated NiO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows lower pre-edge peaks than Ni-foil indicating Ni²⁺ formation; NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 has lower absorption edge and white peak intensity than NiO/Pt₃Ni-400.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inspection of the X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra (Figure 1k) shows that the pre-edge peaks of NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 and NiO/Pt₃Ni-400 are significantly lower than that of Ni-foil, implying that high-spin Ni²⁺ configuration is formed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XAFS shows lower Ni-O and Ni-Ni_ox coordination numbers and intensities in NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 than NiO/Pt₃Ni-400 and NiO; Ni valence states: Pt₃Ni (+1.01), NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 (+1.51), NiO/Pt₃Ni-400 (+1.78), NiO (+2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The intensities of the Ni-O and Ni-Ni_ox signals in the spectrum of NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 are lower than those in the spectra of NiO and NiO/Pt₃Ni-400, suggesting that unsaturated sites exist in NiO/Pt₃Ni-300. Also, the respective average valence states of Pt₃Ni, NiO/Pt₃Ni-300, NiO/Pt₃Ni-400, and NiO (Figure 1n) increase from +1.01, +1.51, +1.78 to +2.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV determines comparable ECSA values for Pt₃Ni, NiO/Pt₃Ni-T series confirming maintained Pt active site exposure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The comparable ECSA values observed for Pt₃Ni, NiO/Pt₃Ni-200, NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 and NiO/Pt₃Ni-400 confirm that NiO deposition takes place with maintenance of Pt active site exposure independent of calcination temperature.

nodes.characterization_summary: CO stripping peak potentials: NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 (0.39 V) < NiO/Pt₃Ni-200 (0.61 V) < Pt₃Ni, NiO/Pt₃Ni-400 (0.65 V), indicating abundant surface OH* on NiO/Pt₃Ni-300.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Analysis of the curves displayed in Figure 3a shows that the CO stripping peak potential of NiO/Pt₃Ni-300(0.39V) is lower than those of Pt₃Ni (0.65 V), NiO/Pt₃Ni-200 (0.61 V), and NiO/Pt₃Ni-400 (0.65 V).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-chronopotentiometry FT-IR shows OH stretching peak at 3380 cm⁻¹ with highest intensity for NiO/Pt₃Ni-300.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast to the pre-chronopotentiometry FT-IR spectrum, the spectrum of the post-chronopotentiometry sample contains a significant peak at 3380 cm⁻¹. This peak corresponds to the stretching vibrations of hydroxyl groups.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ FT-IR during HER shows enhanced H₂O adsorption peak at 3710 cm⁻¹ and stable Cl⁻ peak at 710 cm⁻¹ for NiO/Pt₃Ni-300.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the spectrum of NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 during the HER alkaline simulated seawater (Figure 3f), the H₂O adsorption peak at 3710 cm⁻¹ becomes more intense with the increase in the applied potential from 0 to -0.6 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 has lowest charge transfer resistance (4 Ω alkaline water, 3 Ω alkaline seawater) vs Pt/C (35/55 Ω), Pt₃Ni (10/20 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results indicate that NiO/Pt₃Ni-300 has the lowest charge transfer resistance values (4 and 3Ω compared to commercial Pt/C (35 and 55Ω), Pt₃Ni (10 and 20Ω), NiO/Pt₃Ni-200 (6 and 6Ω), and NiO/Pt₃Ni-400 (5 and 5Ω) in alkaline media and alkaline seawater, respectively.
